newsitem.title: USA: Ascend to buy Cascade for $3.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: Ascend to buy Cascade for $3.7 billion.

text.p: Ascend Communications Inc. stock tumbled Monday morning following its announcement that it is aquiring Cascade Communications Corp. in an effort to broaden its share of the computer networking marketplace.
Ascend plunged by $9.125, or about 18 percent, to $43 in heavy trading on the Nasdaq market, where it and Cascade were the two most actively traded issues.

The descent on Ascend's stock knocked about $650 million from the original value of the stock transaction, which Ascend said was worth about $3.7 billion, based on its stock's closing price of $52 last Thursday.
Cascade added 25 cents to $28.625 -- well below the $36.40 a share that its shareholders were to have received under Ascend's offer, which was announced late Sunday.
Under terms of the definitive agreement, Cascade stockholders were to receive 0.7 of a share of Ascend stock for each Cascade share they own.
Ascend, which is chasing industry leader Cisco Systems Inc., is seeking to acquire Cascade to offer customers a full range of products for linking computer systems.

The combined company, which will keep the Ascend name, will also be able to offer a number of products to companies that provide access to the Internet, the global computer network whose popularity is growing at dazzling speed.

Ascend said it would take an unspecified one-time charge in its third quarter for costs related to the merger, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests to qualify as a tax-free reorganization.

"Ascend and Cascade share a common vision of an emerging network infrastructure that delivers end-to-end networking solutions to a broad base of customers," Ascend President Mory Ejabat said in a statement released late Sunday.

"The combination of the products, technologies and sales channels of both companies, with the leadership each company has in the different market segments, will position the new Ascend as one of the networking industry's premier providers of end-to-end networking solutions ...," he added.
Ejabat will remain president and CEO of the new company.
Ascend shareholders will own about 65 percent and Cascade shareholders about 35 percent of the combined company, which will be based at Ascend's headquarters in Alameda, Calif.
An spokeswoman for Ascend said that if the deal closed by the end of September, it was expected to detract slightly from earnings this fiscal year but add to profits next year.
She said the size of the charge Ascend would take had not yet been determined.
In a separate announcement, Cascade, based in Westford, Mass., said it expected its earnings and revenues for its first quarter, which ended March 29, will be below analysts' expectations.

Cascade said that based on available information, it estimated first-quarter revenues would be around $90 million and earnings, excluding a one-time charge associated with its acquisition of Sahara Networks Inc., would be in the range of 14 cents to 15 cents per share.
Ascend declined to comment on Cascade's announcement.

Once the acquisition is completed, Ascend said, the company will reorganize into four business units -- multimedia access products, remote products, access and concentrator products and core switching systems.
Cascade President and Chief Executive Dan Smith will join Ascend as executive vice president and general manager of the core switching systems unit, the company said.
Ascend's Bob Dahl will continue to serve as chief financial officer of the company.
